what_happened: After handoff, the ego sped up from 4.2 to 5.9 m/s and drifted left, out of its lane and away from the recorded path, which stays straight and then bears right (the command changes to RIGHT). It moved into the adjacent left lane and its front hit actor 56, which was just ahead in that lane.

On a multi-lane highway at about 8 m/s with a clear lead gap of about 25 m, the policy took over at 4.6 s and its plan (orange) swung left toward the adjacent lane, although the route command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT. It cut into actor 33, which was driving alongside in the left lane, and made front contact at 6.2 s.

On a multi-lane highway with a STRAIGHT command, the policy's plan went left into the next lane, away from the recorded path, which stayed straight in the current lane. The ego was speeding up from 4.2 to 5.8 m/s when it cut left into actor 56, which was driving alongside in that lane, and hit it with its front at 6.7 s.

On a straight multi-lane highway at about 8 m/s, the policy's planned path (orange) bent left toward the next lane while the route stayed straight and later called for RIGHT. The ego drifted about 0.9 m left of the recorded path and its front-left clipped actor 33, which was passing alongside in the left lane. The camera smear in the last frame is just the reconstruction distorting at contact, not the cause.

After handoff, with the command STRAIGHT, the policy planned a lane change to the left (orange path toward actor 15) instead of keeping its lane. It steered left into actor 56, which was driving alongside in the left lane, and hit it with the front at about 6 m/s.

On a straight multi-lane freeway at about 8 m/s, the policy's plan (orange) bent toward the left lane after handoff. The ego drifted about 0.85 m left of the recorded path into vehicle 33, which was coming up alongside in the adjacent left lane, and its front corner hit that car. There was no lead-vehicle problem: the gap ahead stayed above 24 m. The smeared car in the last camera frame is a close-range artifact at impact, not the cause.

On a multi-lane freeway with a RIGHT command, and nothing ahead in its lane, the ego slowly drifted left. It moved away from the recorded path to the right (5 m off by the end) and at 8.4–8.8 m/s it crossed the yellow left edge line onto the median shoulder. The camera showed the edge line clearly before the failure; the smearing appeared only near the end and on the right side.

The ego was told to go STRAIGHT on a multi-lane highway but crept along at about 4–5 m/s, well below traffic speed and 66 m behind where the human driver was at that point. Its planned path wandered left, off the recorded route, until the ego was straddling the lane line. Actor 39, overtaking in the lane to the left, then hit the ego's left rear side, which was sticking into its lane (lateral collision at 11.6s).

On a multi-lane highway with a STRAIGHT command, the policy kept slowing for no reason (6.3→4.0 m/s, now ~68 m behind the recorded car) and its wavy planned path drifted the ego ~1.7 m left toward the lane line. Actor 29, coming up in the adjacent left lane, clipped the ego's left rear side, which logged a lateral collision at 12.0s.
